key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger greatly boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4 while offering a more sustainable alternative to conventional sacrificial agents.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a materials-and-system design route for greener CO2 photoconversion by combining CO2 capture via microalgae with charge-efficient photocatalysis on an engineered HEO.
method: Designed an AB2O6 high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to increase surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption and Bi/Ta/Nb to support polarization and charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion with no sacrificial agent, with microplastics, and with microalgae as the sacrificial agent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on maintaining stable microalgae performance and managing biomass handling, separation, and process integration over time.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
